name: Gerlosberg
kurzbeschreibung: Charming mountain hamlet in the Gerlostal valley, with authentic Tirol charm and stunning tranquility.
beschreibung:
Overview

Gerlosberg is situated at approximately 1,050 metres altitude across the sun-drenched mountain slopes rising directly above Zell am Ziller in the Tyrolean district of Schwaz. The municipal territory stretches from the floor of the Zillertal at around 600 metres up to the 2,558-metre summit of the Kreuzjoch in the Kitzbühel Alps. With around 500 inhabitants, Gerlosberg is a classic dispersed Tyrolean mountain community without a concentrated village core, comprised of sunny hamlets such as Klammegg, Eben, Innerberg, and Erlach. Its elevated hillside location provides breathtaking panoramic views across the central valley basin toward the Tux Alps and glaciated summits. Gerlosberg harmoniously unites pastoral mountain farming life with immediate access to one of the most modern ski areas in the Alps.

History

The settlement of Gerlosberg began in the High Middle Ages through the establishment of permanent alpine dairy farmsteads known as Schwaighöfen. The location was first recorded in 1237 as Gerlaisperch in registers of the Cathedral Chapter of Salzburg. These mountain farms specialised in cattle breeding and cheese production; historic deeds mention privileged holdings such as the Irmstall farm, whose owners were exempt from taxes in exchange for maintaining the vital packhorse trail up to Gerlos. Gold mining on the adjacent slopes of Hainzenberg also influenced the economic life of local families. The municipal coat of arms, granted in 1989, features a golden shield with a black bull's head, symbolising the twin pillars of cattle husbandry and historic mining. Ecclesiastically linked to the parish of Zell am Ziller, the spiritual heart of the community is the heritage-protected Schoolhouse Chapel of the Presentation of Mary, built in 1951 incorporating timber from the historic schoolhouse.

Getting There

By car, visitors travel via the Inntal Autobahn A12 to the Wiesing/Zillertal exit, following the federal road B169 to Zell am Ziller. From the town, the winding Gerlosberg municipal road climbs in sweeping serpentines up the sunny mountain face to the scattered hamlets. Rail passengers arrive at Jenbach station via ÖBB or DB long-distance lines and transfer to the narrow-gauge Zillertalbahn running every half hour to Zell am Ziller. From Zell railway station, regional bus and taxi route 682T provides public transport connections up the mountain, carrying winter guests directly to the mid-station of the Rosenalmbahn gondola.

Tips

A premier highlight of Gerlosberg is direct access to the vast Zillertal Arena ski network: the modern Rosenalmbahn cable car glides right over municipal land up to the Rosenalm at 1,744 metres, providing doorstep access to 150 kilometres of pistes. In summer, the Rosenalm transforms into a family adventure hub featuring the Fichtenschloss (Spruce Castle), a massive wooden playground, and the scenic Lake Fichtensee with swimming, boat hire, and stand-up paddling. Experienced mountaineers hike up to the 2,558-metre Kreuzjoch for an awe-inspiring 360-degree panorama of the Zillertal and Tux Alps. Many traditional heritage farmsteads offer farm-stay accommodation, artisan schnapps tastings, and fresh alpine Graukäse cheese.
